purpose: Independent measured larger-rover points for model comparison; no calibration. Four-wheel Husky and six-wheel SSTB-Lite are reported separately.

demishkevich.title: Experimental Evaluation of Rover Mobility Prediction Methods using Single Wheel Experiments
demishkevich.author: Alexander Demishkevich

fiset.title: Effects of Turning Radius on Skid-Steered Wheeled Robot Power Consumption on Loose Soil
fiset.author: Jean-Sebastien Fiset
fiset.use: Table 3.2 stock Husky geometry: radius 165 mm, width 125 mm. Assumed stock-wheel match to Demishkevich; not an additional slope/slip campaign.

zhou.title: Simulations of Mars Rover Traverses
zhou.use: Only actual measured diamond markers from Figure 13; none of the Artemis simulation curves.

cases.label: Husky, stock rubber tires
cases.geometry_status: Stock dimensions from Fiset Table 3.2 assumed applicable; Demishkevich does not explicitly give absolute stock tire dimensions. Its reported D/W=2.63 is consistent with these dimensions within rounding.
cases.soil: GRC-1 simulant, 28-31% relative density, cone-index gradient 3.9-4.3
cases.measurement: Table 4.10, Full Rover Results row, printed page 53 / PDF page 65. Total-station actual motion versus commanded motion. Two trials per slope in section 4.4.3; no raw repeats or standard deviations recovered.

cases.label: Husky, rigid grouser wheels
cases.geometry_status: Outer diameter including grousers; Figure 3.5 and section 3.2. 300 mm outer / 268 mm nominal wheel scaled by 1.28.
cases.soil: GRC-1 simulant, 28-31% relative density, cone-index gradient 3.9-4.3
cases.measurement: Table 4.8, Full Rover Results row, printed page 51 / PDF page 63. Two trials per slope, steady-state average. Table 3.2 lists 0.8116 rad/s and 0.1392 m/s, consistent with nominal radius 171.5 mm rather than grouser-tip radius 192 mm.
cases.slip_reference_status: Nominal-radius interpretation of commanded speed; also retain unconverted published slip. It cannot change the finding that the extrapolated model is physically invalid.

cases.label: SSTB-Lite, Dumont Dunes
cases.campaign: Zhou et al. 2014, field measurements made May 2012
cases.geometry_status: MER spare wheel radius 13.1 cm and width 16 cm, section 4.1; section 4.2 uses the MER-derived SSTB-Lite. Grouser height 6 mm, 31 grousers. A +12 mm diameter sensitivity covers the nominal-versus-tip interpretation.
cases.soil: Dumont Dunes, well-sorted, well-rounded natural sand
cases.measurement: Figure 13, printed page 153 / PDF page 13, measured slip diamonds only. Rear LEFT wheel uphill, not whole-rover average. Cleat-imprint spacing gives slip, electronic level on rover deck gives slope. Source estimates slip measurement error about 0.6 percentage points; our plot-reading error is additional.

digitization.render: PDF page 13 rendered using pdftoppm -scale-to 2100, original image 1575 x 2100 pixels
digitization.selection: Ten resolved measured diamond markers spanning the displayed slope range. Illustrative point picks, not a complete raw dataset, trial count, or reconstructed population mean. Dense overlapping high-slope markers are not all recovered.

additional_larger_rover_sources.title: Terrain traversability prediction for off-road vehicles based on multi-source transfer learning
additional_larger_rover_sources.usefulness: Measured straight uphill slip at 0.055 m/s across nine surfaces, including loose and compacted sand; Figures 5 and 6. Slope accuracy about 1 degree.
additional_larger_rover_sources.not_scored_reason: Wheel diameter and width not specified in the inspected article. Do not infer them from a photograph. Figure 6 red curves are fitted GP predictions, not measured observations.

additional_larger_rover_sources.title: Vibration-based wheel-terrain slip detection for skid-steer rovers
additional_larger_rover_sources.usefulness: Separate stock-Husky CSA Mars Yard campaign at 0.2 m/s; 27 slope runs in Table 4.3; total-station motion ground truth.
additional_larger_rover_sources.not_scored_reason: Table 4.3 labels low/high slip but does not report numerical slope angles, loaded mass, or wheel dimensions. Induced-slip tables prescribe slip by tethering; they do not validate free-climbing slip.

additional_larger_rover_sources.title: The Canadian Planetary Emulation Terrain Energy-Aware Rover Navigation Dataset
additional_larger_rover_sources.usefulness: Independent instrumented Husky, over 1.2 km of field driving, encoder motion and GPS/visual/IMU trajectory estimates plus terrain maps.
additional_larger_rover_sources.not_scored_reason: Raw data access requires IEEE DataPort login; smallest human-readable base run is 11.2 GB. Exact loaded mass and wheel geometry also need verification. No data or error statistics fabricated.

excluded_from_experimental_validation: Hu et al. 2024, DOI 10.1002/rob.22276: the 108 kg case is a simulated SINGLE WHEEL load, not a measured 108 kg rover.
Nishishita and Ishigami 2025 cargo rover paper: 20-100 kg sweep is simulated, not physical test data.
NASA LROP prove-out paper: slope tests at 31.7 kg total, with qualitative pass/half-pass/fail rather than numerical slip; not part of the requested mass comparison.
Watanabe 1.5 kg and Moonraker 8 kg: excluded from larger-rover assessment as requested.
